metrics.rationale: User specifies CO2 band 4.15–4.35 μm must transmit radiation ('通过二氧化碳 4.15–4.35 μm')
User specifies CO band 4.55–4.75 μm must transmit radiation ('通过一氧化碳 4.55–4.75 μm')
User specifies 3.60–4.00 μm range must suppress background ('在 3.60–4.00 μm 范围内抑制背景')
User specifies 4.85–5.20 μm range must suppress thermal radiation ('4.85–5.20 μm 范围内抑制背景和其他热辐射')

standard.metric_rationale: These four metrics directly map to the user's four wavelength requirements: two passbands (CO2 at 4.15–4.35 μm and CO at 4.55–4.75 μm) requiring high transmittance, and two stopbands (3.60–4.00 μm and 4.85–5.20 μm) requiring high reflectance to block background radiation. Using mean_transmittance for passbands and reflectance_stopband for stopbands matches the semantic intent of '通过' (transmit) versus '抑制' (suppress/block). The maximum of 4 metrics is fully utilized because omitting any band would allow designs to sacrifice that unmeasured requirement. Layer count (≤24), material constraints (no metal, dielectric only), and incidence angle (normal) are manufacturing and physics constraints handled separately, not ranking metrics.
standard.formula_rationale: The user requires two passbands (CO2 at 4.15–4.35 μm and CO at 4.55–4.75 μm) to transmit radiation, and two stopbands (3.60–4.00 μm and 4.85–5.20 μm) to suppress background and thermal radiation. All four metrics carry equal importance because the monitoring system cannot function correctly if any one band fails—missing CO2 transmission breaks CO2 detection, missing CO transmission breaks CO detection, and inadequate suppression in either stopband allows interfering radiation to reach the detector. Since the user stated no preference for weighting one requirement above another, a plain sum treats each band equally. Each term uses the variable directly because all four have 'maximize' direction: higher transmittance in the passbands is better, and higher reflectance in the stopbands is better.
